agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider borrowing bylaw to temporarily finance 2027 spending
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a Temporary Financing Bylaw that would give the City borrowing authority to temporarily finance its 2027 expenditures. In plain terms, this bylaw would let the City borrow money to cover costs until its regular tax and other revenue comes in. It is a routine cash-flow measure, not a new tax or fee on businesses. The bylaw is up for approval at the October 6, 2026 council meeting.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action needed — this is a routine City cash-flow borrowing measure, but watch for the council decision on October 6, 2026.

key_dates.label: Burnaby temporary financing bylaw council decision

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review Burnaby's Housing Accelerator Fund Year 3 progress
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will receive a mid-term status update on the city's Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) program, a federal initiative that gives cities money to speed up home building. The report covers Year 3 progress and a proposed financial plan for HAF spending from 2026 to 2030, with $10.96 million planned for 2026 and $11.04 million for 2027. The city may receive up to $11.2 million in 2027. Council is not voting on a new bylaw at this stage — this is an information report. However, the funding decisions discussed could affect construction timelines, permit processing, and housing development activity in Burnaby over the next several years.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the HAF financial plan — it could affect construction timelines and permit processing in Burnaby.

key_dates.label: Burnaby HAF Year 3 mid-term report to Council

agenda_briefs.title: Council to review Burnaby's 2026 Period 8 financial report
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby's financial report as at Period 8 (January 1 to August 9, 2026) shows a net surplus of $16.2M, driven mainly by higher-than-budgeted building permit fees and new-growth tax revenue. The surplus is forecast to shrink to about $9.1M by year end as compensation, benefits and sick-leave costs rise. Planning revenues are below budget, a leading indicator of weaker permit revenue ahead. The report is received for information only — no decisions or bylaw changes.

key_dates.label: Burnaby Financial Management Committee reviews Period 8 report

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider October 2026 update on Burnaby civic projects
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby's Financial Management Committee will receive a status update on significant civic projects on October 6, 2026. The report details the Mintara Restaurant patio expansion on Burnaby Mountain (a 2,000-square-foot enclosed, all-weather patio with a full bar and barbecue, delayed by guardrail supply issues), the Shadbolt Centre main stage and art studios (handover moved up to Q4 2026, occupancy inspection in early October 2026), and the Burnaby Lake Recreation Centre (handover anticipated Q1 2028, on budget). No new rules or fees are proposed.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Review the October 6, 2026 report and Attachment 1 to see if any civic project affects your business location or permits.

key_dates.label: Burnaby council meeting on civic projects status update
